name: chart-map-02
title: Brazil election 2026
description: First-round presidential results by state, with winning vote-share colours and accessible interactive details. Built with TanStack Charts.

meta.prompt:
# Objective

Build `chart-map-02`, titled “Brazil election 2026”: a responsive, interactive choropleth map of Brazil’s 2026 first-round presidential election results.

Display the heading “Brazil Election 2026”. State colours identify the leading candidate; colour intensity represents that candidate’s share of valid votes. Include a national results chart, state statistics cards, candidate legends, overseas results, and source attribution.

# Dependencies

- React and TypeScript: components, typed election data, and interaction state.
- TanStack Charts: generate geographic shapes and horizontal bar geometry.
- d3-geo: a Mercator projection fitted to Brazil’s boundaries.
- Tailwind CSS: responsive layout, theme tokens, and styling.
- Native CSS transitions: card entrance, exit, selected-card movement, and hover highlighting.

Keep the map, national chart, statistics card, and legends as separate components. Derive display data separately from interaction state.

# Layout and visual design

Arrange the interface in this order:

1. Centred heading.
2. National results chart.
3. Brazil choropleth map.
4. Candidate legends, explanatory text, and overseas results.
5. Source attribution footer.

Use a clean, unboxed layout with generous whitespace. Use theme tokens for surrounding text, borders, and backgrounds. Preserve election colours across light and dark themes.

## National results chart

Show Lula first in red and Flávio Bolsonaro second in blue, followed by a separate Other summary beneath a divider.

Use four aligned columns: candidate name, horizontal bar, vote percentage, and vote count. On small screens, use `100px minmax(0,1fr) 48px 48px` with an 8px gap. From the small breakpoint upwards, use `180px minmax(0,1fr) 72px 72px` with a 16px gap. Use three shared rows for axis headings, candidate results, and the Other/reference-key row.

Use a linear percentage scale from 0% to 75%. Label 0%, 25%, 50%, and 75%. Mark 50% with a vertical line, downward triangle, and TO WIN label. Display compact percentages and million-vote counts to one decimal place. Right-align numeric columns and use tabular numerals. Align Other with the 75% endpoint while preserving its percentage and count columns.

Include REPORTING and FINAL RESULTS reference keys. Use diagonal hatching for reporting swatches and solid candidate colours for final-result swatches. These explain the visual treatment without claiming verified reporting status. Place the wrapping key in column two on desktop, aligned left with the plot; on mobile, place it in column one, aligned right with candidate names.

## Geographic map

Render all 26 states and the Federal District using a shared Mercator projection. Preserve geographic proportions as the map resizes. Use thin white state boundaries, no bubbles, and no Cartesian axes.

Place bold state abbreviations inside large states. Use external labels and leader lines for small or narrow states. External labels activate the same state as its geographic shape.

## Legends and context

Show each leading candidate’s full name above three square swatches labelled Below 50%, 50–60%, and Above 60%.

Display: “Colour shows the leading candidate. Darker shades show a higher share of valid votes.”

Show overseas voting separately in a paragraph beginning with a bold Overseas voting label. Include both main candidates and Other, their percentages, and exact vote counts, separated by semicolons.

On wide screens, position this context block in the open lower-left area of the map. On smaller screens, place it below the map in normal document flow.

# Content and data

Use bundled snapshots without runtime scraping or election-data requests. Join geographic features and election results using stable state identifiers.

- [Wikipedia first-round results, revision 1378844298](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2026_Brazilian_general_election&oldid=1378844298#First_round_results_by_federative_unit), retrieved 2026-10-07.
- [Official IBGE state boundaries](https://servicodados.ibge.gov.br/api/v3/malhas/paises/BR?formato=application/vnd.geo%2Bjson&qualidade=minima&intrarregiao=UF), retrieved 2026-10-07.

Display both source links and retrieval dates in a footer below overseas results. Attribute Wikipedia contributors and link to [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). Source and licence links open in a new tab.

Use the national top two candidates consistently across national, state, and overseas summaries. Aggregate all remaining candidates into Other. Calculate Other’s share from combined votes rather than rounded percentage sums.

National results:

- Flávio Bolsonaro: 47.03%, 56,104,503 votes.
- Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva: 45.16%, 53,879,538 votes.
- Other: 7.81%, 9,316,747 votes.

Use these palettes:

| Candidate | Below 50% | 50–60% | Above 60% |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flávio Bolsonaro | `#a6cdf5` | `#2184d9` | `#154d83` |
| Lula | `#f4a4af` | `#e31837` | `#861225` |

Exactly 50% and 60% belong to the middle band. Determine each state’s leader from all candidates; use neutral grey without a unique leader. Intensity represents the leader’s valid-vote share, not total votes or winning margin. Do not invent reporting percentages or counted-sections figures.

# States and interactions

Maintain separate hovered and selected states. Selection takes precedence over hover preview.

## Initial state

Start with no selected state and no statistics card. Display the complete map and contextual information.

## Hover preview

When no state is selected:

- Pointer entry subtly increases the state’s brightness while preserving its election colour.
- Show its statistics card beside the pointer and track movement immediately.
- Pointer exit removes the highlight and hides the card.
- Do not add a black boundary.

The preview card is non-interactive, uses tooltip semantics, and has no Close button.

## Selection

Clicking, tapping, or keyboard-focusing a state selects it. Enter and Space activate the focused state.

Selection draws a visible black boundary and shows an interactive statistics card with a bottom Close button. Clicking another state transfers selection. While selected, hovering other states still highlights them but never replaces the selected statistics or moves the card.

## Dismissal and keyboard navigation

Clear selection and hide the card on Close, Escape, an empty-area click, or keyboard focus leaving the map and card. Preserve selection while focus moves between a state and its Close button.

Use the forward tab sequence `state → its Close button → next state`, with corresponding reverse navigation through Shift+Tab. Do not trap focus. After Close or Escape, focus a stable map container without immediately reselecting the dismissed state.

# Responsive behaviour

Use a floating card on desktop and mobile. Place it beside its anchor with a 12px horizontal gap. Choose the roomier side, favouring right on a tie. Keep the card inside the intersection of the visible map area and viewport, with an 8px inset. Adjust vertical position and clamp horizontally. Recalculate after scrolling or resizing.

Hover previews anchor to the current pointer position. Click selection freezes the clicked position. Keyboard selection anchors to the state’s visual centre.

Use a maximum width of 220px when the map container is narrower than 640px and 320px otherwise. Constrain width further when necessary. Allow internal scrolling if content exceeds the available height.

## Statistics card

Use a white surface, dark text, subtle border, rounded corners, and soft shadow. Show:

- State name.
- Exact vote lead in the leading candidate’s colour.
- Leading candidate and percentage-point lead.
- The national top two candidates ordered by local votes, followed by Other.
- A colour dot, name, percentage, and exact vote count for each row.
- A full-width bottom Close button only when selected.

Display percentages and point differences to two decimals, and exact counts with thousands separators. On desktop, use approximately 20px padding and a 24px state heading. On mobile, use approximately 10px padding, a 16px state heading, 12px candidate labels, and 10–11px secondary text. Shorten Lula’s visible mobile label to Lula while retaining his full name in its title attribute. Keep Close at least 40px tall.

# Motion and accessibility

Use a 120ms fade and a 4px upward entrance movement. Reverse these for exit. Keep preview pointer tracking immediate without a position transition. When selection transfers between states, animate card position over 120ms. Update content without replaying entrance. Animate hover brightness over 120ms. Disable transitions for reduced-motion preferences.

Expose every state as an individually focusable button with an accessible name, selection information through `aria-pressed`, and a relationship to its statistics card. Use black selection outlines independently of colour.

Give selected cards group semantics and Close a visible keyboard focus indicator. Hidden cards must not remain interactive or exposed to assistive technology. Provide a screen-reader table of exact national percentages and vote counts; hide its duplicate decorative chart from assistive technology.

# Acceptance criteria

- All 27 federative units render and are individually keyboard-accessible.
- Results join to boundaries by stable identifiers.
- No selection or card appears initially.
- Hover previews appear only without selection.
- Hovering another state highlights it while preserving selected statistics.
- Click, tap, and keyboard focus select a state and draw its black boundary.
- Close, Escape, blank-area clicks, and focus leaving dismiss selection.
- Tab follows `state → Close → next state` without trapping focus.
- Cards remain usable within the visible map area on narrow screens.
- Legends match the map’s palettes and thresholds.
- Summaries contain only the top two candidates and Other.
- Sources, retrieval dates, and attribution are visible.
- Reduced-motion preferences disable transitions.

# Keywords

Choropleth map, Mercator projection, GeoJSON, TanStack Charts, SVG, horizontal bar chart, linear scale, categorical band scale, valid-vote share, threshold colour encoding, hover preview, persistent selection, pointer tracking, floating panel, viewport clamping, keyboard navigation, focus management, tooltip, aria-pressed, tabular numerals, opacity transition, translate transition, position transition, reduced motion, responsive layout, bundled snapshot, source attribution.
